deep.reconstruction:
Context (§6 of the 1966-67 'Cristaux' notes). On the previous pages Grothendieck computes H*(X_cris, O) and H*(X_Strat, O) via a cosimplicial 'Čech-type' resolution F^α = (F^(ν))_{ν≥0}, viewed as a cosimplicial sheaf on X_Zar.

Stratifying case. F^(ν) is the structure sheaf of the formal completion X^{ν+1}_{/X} of X^{ν+1} = X×_S…×_S X along the diagonal (or of the PD-envelope of the diagonal, in the crystalline variant). If X is not smooth (case 6.2), one uses an embedding, or a projective system of embeddings X ⊂ Y(i), and replaces X^{ν+1} by Y(i)^{ν+1}.

6.4 states three things.
(1) For F = O_{X_Strat} or O_{X_cris}, each term F^(ν) is a 'coinduced' Ring on X_Zar. In SGA4 terminology this is a sheaf of the form u_*(something) pushed down from the topos of the thickening, hence acyclic for the comparison. In case 6.2 it is the projective limit lim_i F(i)^* of the coinduced rings attached to the thickenings Y(i). Since Y(i)_Zar = X_Zar (the immersions are nilpotent or homeomorphic), everything lives on the single space X_Zar. The study of the complex thus reduces essentially to the stratifying context.
(2) Each F^(ν) is an O_X-algebra in ν+1 canonical ways, via the projections pr_i : X^{ν+1}_{/X} → X. Choosing, say, pr_1 makes F^(ν) a pro-quasi-coherent O_X-algebra, an inverse limit of the quasi-coherent algebras O_{X^{ν+1}}/I^n.
(3) With respect to such a structure, the coface maps, hence the coboundaries of the associated cochain complex, are not O_X-linear. They are differential operators of infinite order, i.e. pro-differential operators such as the Taylor map O_X → \hat O_{X×X}. After decomposing the F^(ν) (e.g. into graded pieces, or using coordinates / Taylor expansion), one obtains ordinary differential operators. This is the familiar linearization picture: the Čech–Alexander complex is a canonical cochain complex, functorial and needing no choice of coordinates or of smoothness. It is in this respect better behaved than the de Rham complex, to which it is quasi-isomorphic when X is smooth (char 0 for the stratifying case, with divided powers for the crystalline case).

The page breaks off mid-sentence comparing these complexes with de Rham complexes. The next page is a crossed-out fragment plus a sketch.

Purpose: computing infinitesimal/crystalline cohomology by an explicit canonical complex. This is preparatory material for Grothendieck's 1966 IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968).
errors: No mathematical error visible. The claim that the cofaces are 'differential operators of infinite order' must be read in the pro-sense, i.e. as continuous maps into pro-quasi-coherent completions. They are not genuine operators of infinite order in the D^† / analytic sense.
The final sentence is incomplete, so the intended comparison with de Rham complexes cannot be fully checked.

ideas.what: Computing H*(X_Strat,O) / H*(X_cris,O) via the cosimplicial complex of the formal (resp. PD) completions of the diagonal in X^{ν+1} or Y^{ν+1}, as a complex of sheaves on X_Zar
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Terms of the resolution are coinduced (pushforward) rings, hence suitable for computing cohomology on X_Zar; non-smooth case handled as a projective limit over embeddings Y(i) with the same Zariski space
ideas.modern_name: acyclicity of coinduced sheaves / reduction via embeddings into smooth schemes (Hartshorne-style completion)

ideas.what: F^(ν) are O_X-algebras in ν+1 ways via the projections; via pr_1 they are pro-quasi-coherent, and the coboundaries are infinite-order (pro-)differential operators that become ordinary differential operators after decomposition
ideas.modern_name: linearization of differential operators; pro-quasi-coherent principal parts P^∞_X

deep.surprise_reason: Draft material for the Čech–Alexander complex and linearization arguments that Grothendieck published in 'Crystals' (1968). Nothing beyond the published account is visible.
transcription_corrections: Margin: 'Cas de O_{X_Strat} et O_{X(cris)}' — consistent with the image.

'Ceci est donc, pour l'étude de ce complexe, ramené essentiellement au contexte stratifiant': the image suggests 'Ceci nous ramène donc, pour l'étude de ce complexe, essentiellement au contexte stratifiant'.
'qui ne sont[?] via[?]' is likely 'qui se font via' or 'qui viennent via' (the projections pr_i); 'via' is fairly clear.
'dans X^{ν+1}_{/X} sur X' — the subscript /X (formal completion along the diagonal) is visible under X^{ν+1}.

Last lines: 'C'est bien vrai que complexes de cochaînes canoniques (plus fait que pour les complexes de De Rham). que les complexes' — 'vrai' is a plausible reading of the word after 'bien'; the sentence is fragmentary.
